situation.summary: Tenant Elowen Marr reported peeling kitchen-cabinet laminate with sharp edges that had caused cuts, and doors that do not close (E001, S:initial-request). The landlord approved only the original laminate-repair scope, which the record shows as an internal note with no landlord message behind it (E006). The contractor has since proposed a full kitchen. On 24 Sep he sent £4,850 supply, £3,800 fitting, £230 waste, all plus VAT, and a £380 electrical estimate (E024), with no cupboards-and-doors-only estimate. Nia forwarded these figures to the landlord at 14:36 (E025), and the landlord has not replied. The commission basis, any cap and the payable total remain unresolved (E022, E023). No visit has taken place in 20 days, and the tenant has had no update since 9 Sep (E008).
situation.task: Decide the next step on the kitchen-cabinet repair now that a full-kitchen replacement quote has arrived, outside the approved laminate-repair scope, with the commission basis unsettled.
situation.stageLabel: Full-kitchen quote forwarded to landlord (E025); awaiting landlord decision on a replacement scope that is not approved; laminate-repair approval only; commission basis and payable total unconfirmed
situation.whoseMove: Our move first, not the landlord's. (1) The commission basis, cap, VAT treatment and payable total (E022, E023) need a person with authority before any figure is treated as final. This is a revised price beyond the approved scope and an instruction the record does not support, so it should go to a human (case.escalate). (2) The tenant has had no update since 9 Sep and was given no safety guidance about the sharp edges. A tenant.update should go in the same turn: status, what happens next, a date for our next update, and a request for new dog-safe access windows. Landlord (Soren Pike): decision on the full-kitchen figures is pending (E025); no chase is due until about 27 Sep, three days after E025. Contractor (Kellan Rook): owes the cupboards-and-doors-only estimate, which was never explicitly requested from him (E018 asked only for a full-kitchen quote), and a visit slot. Both need our instruction, not the landlord's.

decision.actionLabel: Ask Alderline Joinery for the cupboards-and-doors-only estimate the landlord requested, and confirm the full-kitchen figures are firm
decision.message:
Hi Kellan,

Thank you for the full-kitchen figures for 42 Brackenveil Row, Oakhollow, received today. I have passed them to the landlord.

The landlord asked for estimates for two options, so they can compare them:
1. Full new kitchen. Received: supply £4,850 + VAT; removal and fitting, including tiled splashback, £3,800 + VAT; waste removal £230 + VAT; electrical work estimated at £380 + VAT, to be checked.
2. Replacement cupboards and doors only, keeping the existing appliances, worktops and flooring, which the landlord says are in good condition. We do not have this one yet. My earlier email asked only for the full-kitchen price, so I am sorry that this was not clear. Please send an itemised estimate for this option, with VAT shown on each line, along with photos and an estimated completion time.

Please also confirm in writing:
- that the figures for both options are the full amounts you would invoice, with nothing further to be added once our commission arrangement is applied. If anything is still to be settled on your side, please tell me now rather than at invoice stage;
- whether you need to visit the property to confirm either price. If you do, I will arrange a time with the tenant. There are two dogs at the property, and they must be secured before anyone goes in.

To be clear, this is a request for an estimate only. The landlord has not approved either replacement option, so please do not order materials or book any work.

Please reply by Friday 26 September. If anything stops you sending the estimate by then, let me know the date you can send it.

Kind regards,
Nia Calder
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord asked for two options, a full kitchen and cupboards and doors only (E016), and we confirmed both would be reported back (E017). But the request to the contractor asked only for the full kitchen (E018), and only those figures arrived (E024). The landlord now has one option (E025) when he asked to compare two, so his decision may wait on the missing estimate. Only the contractor can supply it. This is a new request, not a repeat of an earlier one, so it can go now. The contractor also said the commission basis could change his quoted amount (E022). The call that followed did not settle a total (E023). Under the rule that a go-ahead is relayed only against a firm figure, we need written confirmation that the figures are final before the landlord approves anything. It is too soon to chase the landlord: E025 went out minutes before this snapshot. Escalation is not needed yet. No spend is being approved, and the immediate gap is something the contractor can fill. The tenant reported cuts from sharp edges (E001) and has heard nothing since 9 September (E008), so they get an update and interim safety advice in the same turn.
decision.expectedOutcome: The contractor sends an itemised cupboards-and-doors-only estimate and confirms whether the figures are firm, or says a visit is needed. Both options then go to the landlord together for a decision. The tenant knows the status, how to stay safe meanwhile, and when they will next hear from us.

final.rationale: The full-kitchen quote reached the landlord one minute before the snapshot (E025), so it is too early to chase him; the 3-day mark falls on Saturday 27 Sep, so the next working day is Monday 29 Sep. A new question is not a chase, though, and there is one. On 10 Sep the landlord asked for two estimates: a full kitchen, and cupboards and doors only (E016). Nia confirmed she would report back on both (E017), but her request to the contractor asked only for the full kitchen (E018), and the figures he sent cover only that (E024). The landlord cannot compare the options until the second estimate exists, and only the contractor can provide it. The contractor also said the commission basis, any cap and VAT could change his figures (E022), and that was not settled (E023). Under the refinements, price and scope must be firm before a go-ahead is relayed, so we ask him now to confirm the figures in writing. This is not an escalation. Nothing has been approved, there is no complaint, and nobody has asked for spend. The agency's internal commission arrangement may need a person later, but today the contractor can simply confirm whether his figures are final. The tenant reported cuts (E001) and has heard nothing since 9 Sep (E008), so she gets a status update, interim safety advice and a date. The landlord gets a short note so he does not approve figures that may change.
final.expectedOutcome: By 29 Sep the contractor sends the cupboards-and-doors estimate, or says when he will visit to price it, and confirms whether the full-kitchen figures are final. We then send both options to the landlord together, with VAT stated, for his decision.
boundaries: Asking for an estimate does not approve either replacement option or any spend.
